script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'hail-b2-build',
  description: 'Build B2 of the hail history: reports, radar detections, warnings, zone products and station gusts joined into the sheet and town tables; three builders, four reviewers, skeptics, fixers, re-check',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Build', detail: 'joins module and job; site; docs' },
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'data correctness, browser, rules and words, job and determinism' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'one skeptic per finding' },
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'fixers by ownership' },
    { title: 'Recheck', detail: 'tests, builds, smoke, record' },
  ],
}

const WT = '/home/user/wt/wt-b2'
const BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-b2-brief.md'
const B1BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-build-brief.md'
const RESEARCH = '/home/user/wt/wt-hail/research/hail-history'
const OUT = '/home/user/hail-b2/out'
const STORE_TAR = '/home/user/hail-b1/out2/store/hail-store.tar.gz'
const STORE_DIR = '/home/user/hail-b1/out2/store/store'
const VENV = '/home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python'

const COMMON = `You work in the git worktree ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b2, based on claude/hail-b1 at 7aec754, which holds B1 and main). Read ${BRIEF} in full first: it is the contract (sources, kinds, radii, data layout, words, job, gates, ownership). Then read ${B1BRIEF} decisions 1 to 16, docs/DECISIONS.md D34 and docs/DESIGN.md section 9 in the worktree, website/hail.py and the hail section of website/static/map/map.js, and the research evidence under ${RESEARCH}/validation-evidence/ named in the brief (read-only; it is another worktree). Repository rules (AGENTS.md is in your context): Python first (every word the viewer reads is written in Python; the browser fetches, filters by distance, fills templates and lists), evidence honesty (kinds apart; never damage, all-clear, insurance, eligibility; missing said as missing), feed contracts (a CONTRACTS row per source, changed with the parser and tests), real-browser checks, plain wording in sentence case, no em-dashes, no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names in repository files (branch names excepted), tests with every behaviour change, no new pip package for the site build (pyshp only in the daily job and in joins.py behind a lazy import). Before building on a source make one live request and check the content, not just HTTP 200; record what you saw in your report. Edit only the files you own (the brief's ownership list); other builders edit other files in the same worktree now, so never run git checkout, stash, reset, add, commit or push, never reformat a file you do not own, and never delete anything outside a folder you created under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ (a test's clean-up wiped the shared temp area on 2026-10-18; tests delete only folders they created). The real B1 store is at ${STORE_DIR} (and ${STORE_TAR}); a python with pyarrow is ${VENV}. Network is available. Return a plain report: what you built, the live requests you made and what their content showed, the commands you ran with results and measured numbers, and anything not done or needing a decision.`

const JOINS = `${COMMON}

You are builder 1, the joins builder. You own website/joins.py (new), tests/test_joins.py (new), .github/workflows/hail-store.yml and website/data/hail-fixture/ (add j/, z/ and s/ files for its three tiles with real rows from your real build; keep the whole fixture under 50 KB; regenerate index.json and manifest.json through hail.py's fixture path or a documented extension of it, and keep hail.py untouched unless a one-line hook is unavoidable, in which case say exactly what you changed). Build website/joins.py: (1) the pulls with a download cache directory (--cache): IEM LSR by month; NCEI Storm Events yearly details files (read the directory listing for the current names; cache by name); SWDI nx3hail by month with the Montana bbox (drop exact duplicate rows); IEM watchwarn polygons per year per phenomenon (SV, TO, FF; limitps=1; issuance polygons; skip EXP and county rows); the NWS public forecast zone shapefile (find the current edition's file name on weather.gov's GIS shapefile page; cache it); IEM zone-based products per year per phenomenon (verify live which request form returns zone rows with UGC; if none works within your attempts, implement the data path and mark the part "unavailable" with the reason, so the sheet says so); IEM daily summaries for the MT_ASOS stations (station list from IEM's network JSON or the research record) per station-year; re-pull windows: the last 2 months (LSR, SWDI), the current year (warnings, zone products, station days), a new file name (NCEI); every request through one HTTP helper with a user agent, retries, and a ledger (ledger/joins.jsonl: url, status, bytes, cache hit); (2) the parsers with the units and conventions in the brief (LSR MAG "None" is missing; NCEI local time MST-7 to UTC; SWDI MAXSIZE hundredths of an inch as an integer; polygon tags as the archive gives them); (3) the joins: a tile's reports and records within 5 miles of its bounds, detections within 2 miles of its bounds (haversine), the warnings whose issuance polygon covers at least one Montana cell of the tile with the 100-bit cover (even-odd point-in-polygon of cell centres, numpy), the zone of every Montana cell (point-in-polygon against the zone shapefile, numpy, vectorised per polygon), the two nearest stations within 40 miles of the tile centre; (4) the writers: hail/j/<tile>.json for every tile the store has, hail/z/<zone>.json, hail/s/<id>.json, the index "joins" block, the manifest entries (read and extend hail/manifest.json; keep hail.py's manifest format), partial and unavailable states per source; (5) verify (counts, the Benchland gate rows, manifest hashes, integers only, every tile has a j/ file) and compare (the research counts, as the brief's gate 2 lists them, with the explanation of deviations); (6) WORDS_JOINS (every sentence and template of the brief's Words section), describe_joins(index, tile_doc, cell_row, cell_col, now, sample) returning the six sections rendered in Python for the town pages, map_data_joins(index) for map.json["hail"]["joins"] (the templates, the radii, the state and the lag); (7) the CLI: python -m website.joins build|verify|compare|fixture. Then write tests/test_joins.py with fixtures for every parser and the join rules (distance edge cases, the 100-bit cover, zone lookup, the unavailable path, forbidden terms over WORDS_JOINS with the allowed type words, the units), and run them. Then RUN the real build: python -m website.joins build --store ${OUT}/joins/store --cache ${OUT}/joins/cache --procs 4 after copying ${STORE_DIR} to ${OUT}/joins/store (cp -r), then verify and compare; measure wall time, bytes of j/, z/ and s/, the largest j/ file, the request counts and cache hits, and run the build a second time from the same cache into a second folder and diff -r the j/, z/ and s/ trees (byte-identical expected). Tar the result as ${OUT}/joins/hail-store.tar.gz (tar czf ... -C store hail) for the site builder and reviewers. Update .github/workflows/hail-store.yml per the brief (the joins step, pyshp, the joins cache, the paths filter). Report the Benchland gate rows you found (the LSR 1.75 in report, the NCEI record, the warnings, the zone, the stations).`

const SITE = `${COMMON}

You are builder 2, the site builder. You own website/build.py, website/sources.py, website/templates/ (map.html, town.html, about.html), website/static/map/map.js, website/static/map/map.css, tools/smoke_map.py, tests/test_site.py and .github/workflows/website.yml. Builder 1 is writing website/joins.py now with this public API (names fixed by the brief): WORDS_JOINS, describe_joins(index, tile_doc, row, col, now, sample=False) -> dict of six sections, map_data_joins(index) -> dict, and the j/, z/, s/ file formats in the brief; read the module as it appears (poll every 2 minutes, up to 40 minutes, for describe_joins and map_data_joins to exist before your integration tests; meanwhile build the templates, the browser code and the smoke checks against the brief's formats). Build: (1) build.py: with --hail-history, copy hail/j, hail/z and hail/s from the store into the site (hail_store already copies hail/; make sure the new folders are included and listed in the manifest check), add map.json["hail"]["joins"] from map_data_joins, and for each town render describe_joins for its cell into town["hail"]["joins"] (reading the tile's j/ file, the zone file and the station files from the copied store), with the unavailable state when the index says a part did not load; the flag-off build must stay byte-identical to the base except shared static assets and their hashes; (2) sources.py: six CONTRACTS rows (lsr, ncei_storm_events, swdi_nx3hail, nws_warnings_polygons, nws_zone_products, asos_daily_gusts) with units, timing, cadence, missing rules and the known gaps, gated like hail_history; (3) templates: the sheet gains the six sections (headings carry the kind word; a list per section; "show all" when a section has more than 10 rows, as a details element the build writes, no new script duty beyond toggling), the town page gains the six tables, the About page gains the paragraph on the kinds joined and the sources not joined; (4) map.js: after the hail shard, fetch the tile's j/ file (same tile name under hail/j/), filter reports and records by haversine distance from the cell centre (5 miles, computed from map.json values: the radii and the earth radius come from the data, not literals), detections within 2 miles, warnings whose cover bit for the cell key is set, the cell's zone from the j/ file's zones map then fetch hail/z/<zone>.json, the stations list then fetch hail/s/<id>.json for each (at most two), format dates and times in Montana time from UTC strings the build wrote (use the browser's time zone formatting with the zone name from map.json), fill WORDS_JOINS templates, render the six sections; the unavailable and no-report sentences from the templates; document the duty in the header; no literal sentence, unit, radius or threshold in map.js (a test greps for the brief's words and numbers); (5) tools/smoke_map.py: on the real store build, the gate cell (row 797, col 1986) sheet shows the six sections with the Benchland LSR 1.75 in row and at least one TFX warning; a no-join cell shows the no-report sentences; request log stays on-site; (6) tests in tests/test_site.py for the templates, the flag-off identity, the contract rows, the map.js literal scan, the town tables from the fixture, the unavailable state. Build and check: python -m unittest tests.test_site; python -m website.build --out ${OUT}/site/off --sample --now 2026-10-18T12:00:00Z; --hail-history --sample into ${OUT}/site/sample (the fixture gains j/, z/ and s/ files from builder 1; until then your sample build must still work with a store lacking them, showing the unavailable sentences); when ${OUT}/joins/hail-store.tar.gz exists (poll every 2 minutes up to 60 minutes), --hail-history --sample --hail-store that tar into ${OUT}/site/real and run PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium python tools/smoke_map.py on each build (--shots on the real one). Report what you changed and measured.`

const DOCS = `${COMMON}

You are builder 3, the docs builder. You own docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, README.md, AGENTS.md and research/hail-history/validation-evidence/b2-verification.json (new). Write: D35 "Hail history B2: the other kinds of evidence in the same sheet (2026-10-18)" after D34: the owner decisions it serves (2, 6, 4, 7, quoted from D34 by number, not re-quoted), the six sources with their kind words, radii, units and known gaps, the sources not joined and why (SPC derives from the LSRs; HRRR is a model; DAT is a damage survey and this site does not state damage), the data layout (j/, z/, s/ files, the index block, the manifest), the daily job's joins step and its cache, the states (loaded, partial, unavailable) and the rule that a failed part is said, the words' honesty rules (kinds apart; a report is not an inspection; tags are the forecast threat; a detection is not hail on the ground; a zone product covers the zone; a station reading is at the station), the time convention (Montana time from UTC; NCEI's MST-7 conversion), and *Why:* in the house style. DESIGN.md section 9: the six sections' states and words, the data contract additions, the browser duty (two to four fetches per click, distance filter, template fill). ROADMAP: the B2 row under Done with "measured in the re-check" where numbers are pending, and B3 and B4 next. README and AGENTS: the joins module in the layout and the job's step. The verification record skeleton with gates B2-1 to B2-9 from the brief, status pending. Em-dashes 0 in your lines; no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names; no invented measurements. Report the diff stat of your files.`

const FIX_DECISIONS = `SUPERVISOR DECISIONS AFTER REVIEW ROUND 1 (2026-10-18; they override the brief where they differ; the brief file now carries them as D1 to D14 under "Supervisor decisions after review round 1"): read that section of ${BRIEF} in full before applying any finding, and apply the findings in the light of those decisions (a finding that asks for a choice is decided there; a finding that contradicts a decision is skipped with the decision cited).`

const FINDINGS = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' }, file: { type: 'string' }, line: { type: 'integer' }, claim: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' }, fix: { type: 'string' },
      severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocking', 'should', 'minor'] }, confidence: { type: 'number' } },
      required: ['id', 'file', 'line', 'claim', 'evidence', 'fix', 'severity', 'confidence'] } },
    measurements: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true },
    gates: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { gate: { type: 'string' }, status: { type: 'string', enum: ['pass', 'fail', 'not_checked'] }, evidence: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['gate', 'status', 'evidence'] } },
    summary: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['findings', 'measurements', 'gates', 'summary'],
}
const VERDICT = { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, refuted: { type: 'boolean' }, reason: { type: 'string' }, fix_ok: { type: 'boolean' }, adjusted_fix: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'refuted', 'reason', 'fix_ok', 'adjusted_fix'] }

const REVIEW_COMMON = `Read-only reviewer in ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b2). Read ${BRIEF} first (the contract and gates B2-1 to B2-9), then ${B1BRIEF} decisions 1 to 16. The research evidence is under ${RESEARCH}/validation-evidence/ (read-only). Never edit, stage, commit or push; scratch only under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ which you create; never delete anything outside it. Report concrete defects only, each with file, line, evidence (command output or quoted text) and an exact minimal fix; rank blocking first; fill the gates you checked; put every measured number in measurements.`

const REVIEWERS = [
  { key: 'data', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: data correctness of the joins. Read website/joins.py and tests/test_joins.py in full. Then, on the built store at ${OUT}/joins/store (or rebuild into your scratch from ${STORE_DIR} with the cache at ${OUT}/joins/cache): (1) independently re-pull one month of LSRs, one month of SWDI and one year of SV polygons live and compare counts with the ledger and the shards; (2) gate B2-2 counts against the research facts (point-reports-archives.json f16, f26, f27, f35; swdi.json f15; warnings-archive.json f8, f9; wind-history.json f24) with the window explained; (3) gate B2-1: find the Benchland LSR 1.75 in report (2025-06-15 20:10 UTC, 47.08 N 110.02 W) in the gate cell's tile file and check its distance from cell (797,1986); the NCEI record; the TFX warnings' covers (compare with warnings-archive.json f32 at 47.0,-109.9); the zone of the gate cell and its high wind warnings; (4) units: LSR hail inches, gusts mph, NCEI knots and mph conversion, SWDI hundredths, tags; NCEI MST-7 to UTC conversion on five sampled rows against the raw file; (5) the 100-bit covers: for 20 random warnings recompute point-in-polygon for the tile's cells with an independent even-odd routine; (6) zones: 200 random Montana cells' zones against an independent point-in-polygon on the shapefile; (7) determinism: two builds from the same cache give byte-identical j/, z/, s/; (8) verify and compare run and pass; (9) every tile has a j/ file; integers only where the format says integers.` },
  { key: 'browser', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: the site in Chromium (rule 8). Build from a copy of the worktree (cp -r without .git into ${OUT}/browser/src): flag-off --sample --now 2026-10-18T12:00:00Z into ${OUT}/browser/off, --hail-history --sample into ${OUT}/browser/sample, --hail-history --sample --hail-store ${OUT}/joins/hail-store.tar.gz into ${OUT}/browser/real, and the base (git -C ${WT} archive 7aec754 | tar -x -C ${OUT}/browser/base-src) flag-off into ${OUT}/browser/base-off; diff -rq base-off vs off: only static/map/map.js, static/map/map.css and ?v= lines in pages may differ. Serve the real build and with Playwright (PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium; read tools/smoke_map.py for the harness) run tools/smoke_map.py and quote the result; then your probes: the gate cell (centre of row 797, col 1986) sheet shows six sections with the Benchland 1.75 in report row, an NCEI record, at least one TFX warning with its tags, the zone name with its products, and station gusts with distances; a cell with no joins shows the no-report sentences in every section; every request goes to the local server only and lists which files were fetched per click (expect hail/t, hail/j, hail/z, hail/s); screenshots at 390x844 and 1280x800, light and dark, into ${OUT}/browser/shots, open them and describe (legible, no overflow, sections in order); town pages: Billings' tables match an independent read of the shards; smoke_pages on the real build; the flag-off build has no joins markup; read map.js's new code and list any literal sentence, unit, radius or threshold (none expected; formatting constants allowed).` },
  { key: 'rules', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: repository rules and words over the whole diff (git -C ${WT} diff 7aec754 --stat, the full diff, untracked files). Check: Python first (every viewer word in Python; the browser filters and fills); evidence honesty (no damage statement except the LSR and NCEI type words next to "report" or "record"; no all-clear, insurance, eligibility; missing said as missing; the kind word in every section heading and row); the six contract rows match the parsers and the brief (units, timing, cadence, missing rules, gaps); tests exist for every behaviour change and python -m unittest discover -s tests passes (run it with ${VENV} and quote the tail) and python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload passes; the daily workflow is sound (joins step order, pyshp install, cache, paths filter) and the YAML parses; docs match what was built (D35, DESIGN, ROADMAP, README, AGENTS make no unmeasured claim); em-dashes in added lines 0; the words Claude, Anthropic, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenAI, Copilot, Gemini, the worker model, the larger model, the mid model in added lines only inside branch names; plain wording and sentence case; no new pip package for the site build (pyshp only in the job and behind a lazy import); the fixture under 50 KB; decision 7 audit: every rmtree, unlink or os.remove under tests/ acts on a folder the test created; the time convention (Montana time from UTC; NCEI MST-7) is applied and stated.` },
  { key: 'job', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: the daily job and the live sources. (1) Simulate the job's steps locally in order in your scratch: copy ${STORE_DIR} to a store folder, run python -m website.joins build with an EMPTY cache (measure wall time and bytes downloaded from the ledger), then verify, then tar; compare the j/, z/ and s/ trees with ${OUT}/joins/store (byte-identical expected except index built_at); (2) check the request behaviour: user agent set, retries, the re-pull windows (last 2 months LSR and SWDI, current year warnings and station days, NCEI by file name), the ledger records every request; (3) the failure paths: with the network blocked for one source (patch the HTTP helper or use a fake), the build marks that part unavailable with the reason, the other parts load, verify passes with the partial state, and the index says so; (4) the IEM and NCEI terms: attribution sentences in the About page and the contract rows match the research terms (warnings-archive.json terms, swdi.json f28, point-reports-archives.json terms); (5) the YAML: parse it; the step order (hail build, joins build, verify both, tar, release); timeout fits the measured time with margin; (6) the SWDI known-gap statement and the NCEI lag sentence render from the index values, not from literals.` },
]

const OWNERSHIP = {
  joins: ['website/joins.py', 'tests/test_joins.py', 'tests/test_hail.py', 'website/hail.py', '.github/workflows/hail-store.yml', 'website/data/hail-fixture/'],
  site: ['website/build.py', 'website/sources.py', 'website/templates/', 'website/static/map/map.js', 'website/static/map/map.css', 'tools/smoke_map.py', 'tests/test_site.py', '.github/workflows/website.yml'],
  docs: ['docs/', 'README.md', 'AGENTS.md', 'research/hail-history/validation-evidence/b2-verification.json'],
}
function ownerOf(file) {
  for (const [k, prefixes] of Object.entries(OWNERSHIP)) if (prefixes.some((p) => file.startsWith(p) || file.includes(p))) return k
  return 'site'
}

phase('Build')
const builds = await parallel([
  () => agent(JOINS, { label: 'build:joins', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
  () => agent(SITE, { label: 'build:site', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
  () => agent(DOCS, { label: 'build:docs', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
])
const [joinsR, siteR, docsR] = builds
log(`builders done: joins ${joinsR ? 'ok' : 'null'}, site ${siteR ? 'ok' : 'null'}, docs ${docsR ? 'ok' : 'null'}`)

phase('Review')
const reviews = await pipeline(
  REVIEWERS,
  (r) => agent(`${r.prompt}\n\nBuilder reports for context (claims to check, not facts):\nJOINS: ${(joinsR || 'none').slice(0, 7000)}\nSITE: ${(siteR || 'none').slice(0, 6000)}\nDOCS: ${(docsR || 'none').slice(0, 3000)}`, { label: `review:${r.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS, model: WORKER }),
  async (result, r) => {
    if (!result) return { key: r.key, findings: [], measurements: {}, gates: [], summary: 'reviewer returned nothing' }
    const fs = result.findings.map((f, i) => ({ ...f, id: `${r.key}-${i + 1}` }))
    log(`${r.key}: ${fs.length} findings`)
    const verdicts = await parallel(fs.map((f) => () =>
      agent(`You are a skeptic checking one review finding in ${WT} (read-only; never edit, stage, commit or push; scratch only under ${OUT}/skeptic-${f.id}/ which you create; never delete anything outside it). The finding:\n${JSON.stringify(f, null, 1)}\n\nOpen the file at the line, reproduce the observation yourself, and read ${BRIEF} for the contract. The finding stands only if the defect is real, matters to the gates or the repository rules (AGENTS.md), and the proposed fix is correct and minimal and introduces nothing unsupported (no new number, no em-dash, no model or AI-product name, no new pip package for the site build, no scope widening, no contradiction of the brief). If the defect is real but the fix is wrong or too broad, set fix_ok false and give an adjusted_fix. Default to refuted=true when uncertain.`,
        { label: `verify:${f.id}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT, model: WORKER })
        .then((v) => (v ? { ...f, verdict: v } : null))))
    return { key: r.key, findings: verdicts.filter(Boolean), measurements: result.measurements, gates: result.gates, summary: result.summary }
  },
)

const all = reviews.flatMap((r) => r.findings)
const confirmed = all.filter((f) => !f.verdict.refuted).map((f) => ({ id: f.id, file: f.file, line: f.line, claim: f.claim, evidence: f.evidence, severity: f.severity, fix: f.verdict.fix_ok ? f.fix : f.verdict.adjusted_fix, owner: ownerOf(f.file) })).filter((f) => f.fix && f.fix.length > 0)
const refuted = all.filter((f) => f.verdict.refuted).map((f) => ({ id: f.id, file: f.file, claim: f.claim, reason: f.verdict.reason }))
log(`confirmed ${confirmed.length} (blocking ${confirmed.filter((f) => f.severity === 'blocking').length}), refuted ${refuted.length}`)

phase('Fix')
const groups = ['joins', 'site', 'docs'].map((k) => ({ k, items: confirmed.filter((f) => f.owner === k) })).filter((g) => g.items.length)
const fixReports = await parallel(groups.map((g) => () =>
  agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${FIX_DECISIONS}\n\nYou are the fixer for the ${g.k} files; you own exactly: ${OWNERSHIP[g.k].join(', ')}. Apply these confirmed findings with exact, minimal edits that keep every public name and the brief's contract. Skip and report any finding naming a file you do not own. After editing run python -m unittest tests.test_joins tests.test_site (and the full suite if you changed joins.py or build.py); if a fix changes the j/, z/ or s/ format or the joins, rebuild ${OUT}/joins/store from ${STORE_DIR} with the cache at ${OUT}/joins/cache and re-tar ${OUT}/joins/hail-store.tar.gz, and say so. Report applied ids, skipped ids with reasons, and the test tail.\n\nFINDINGS:\n${JSON.stringify(g.items, null, 1)}`,
    { label: `fix:${g.k}`, phase: 'Fix', model: WORKER })))

phase('Recheck')
const recheck = await agent(`${REVIEW_COMMON} ${FIX_DECISIONS} You are the final checker. Gate B2-1 reads per decision D1 (two cells). Run and quote: ${VENV} -m unittest discover -s tests (tail); python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload; builds from a copy of the worktree (cp -r without .git into ${OUT}/recheck/src): --sample --now 2026-10-18T12:00:00Z into ${OUT}/recheck/off, --hail-history --sample into ${OUT}/recheck/sample, --hail-history --sample --hail-store ${OUT}/joins/hail-store.tar.gz into ${OUT}/recheck/real; PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium python tools/smoke_map.py on each (--shots on the real one) and tools/smoke_pages.py on the real one; du -sb of hail/j, hail/z, hail/s in the real build and of each _site; the largest j/ file; python -m website.joins verify and compare on ${OUT}/joins/store; git -C ${WT} status --short and diff --stat 7aec754; em-dash and banned-name counts over added lines; a grep of the built real pages for an unfilled brace inside hail sections; the decision 7 audit. Then update research/hail-history/validation-evidence/b2-verification.json in ${WT} (the one file you may edit): each gate's status and evidence from what you measured, measurements, and the confirmed findings applied and refuted ones (ids, one line each) under notes. Return the gate table and measurements as JSON text.`,
  { label: 'recheck', phase: 'Recheck', model: WORKER })

return { joinsR: (joinsR || '').slice(0, 8000), siteR: (siteR || '').slice(0, 6000), docsR: (docsR || '').slice(0, 3000), reviews: reviews.map((r) => ({ key: r.key, summary: r.summary, gates: r.gates, measurements: r.measurements })), confirmed, refuted, fixReports, recheck }

result.joinsR:

**What I built (builder 1, joins)**
